license.note: The compilation (selection, grouping, grade placement and descriptions) is CC BY 4.0. The Dolch words themselves are public domain. Grade placement is a typical guide: programs and standards differ, and it is not a diagnosis.

citeAs: Dyslexia Steps (2026). Word lists by grade, Pre-K to Grade 3, with placement basis. dyslexiasteps.com/word-lists-by-grade. CC BY 4.0.

dolch.summary: Dolch's grade levels for his basic sight vocabulary (public domain).

rf-k-2a.summary: Kindergarten: recognize and produce rhyming words.

rf-k-2c.summary: Kindergarten: blend and segment onsets and rimes (the vowel-plus-ending part) of one-syllable spoken words.

rf-k-2d.summary: Kindergarten: isolate the sounds in three-sound consonant-vowel-consonant words and link the short vowel sounds to their common spellings.

rf-1-2b.summary: Grade 1: blend spoken sounds into one-syllable words, including consonant blends (the standard covers spoken sounds, not print).

rf-1-3a.summary: Grade 1: know the spelling-sound patterns for common consonant digraphs.

rf-1-3b.summary: Grade 1: decode regularly spelled one-syllable words (nonsense words test exactly this).

rf-1-3c.summary: Grade 1: know final -e and common vowel team conventions for long vowels; Grade 2: tell long and short vowels apart, learn additional vowel teams and decode two-syllable words with long vowels.

typical.summary: Common placement in structured literacy programs. No standard names it, and programs differ.
